scope_note: Public-source follow-up for Expedient's adaptive reuse of the pre-existing data-center building at 4777 W Ironwood Drive. Opening-day and current operator specifications are retained as separate dated snapshots because the reported floor-area and critical-load figures changed. Milwaukee County's public tax portal establishes the parcel's tax-year 2025 net property tax and matching paid amount, but not the allocation of those receipts to Expedient rather than the parcel owner. The 2022 real-estate sale, parcel assessments, permit values, property-tax payment, and hiring plan remain distinct measures: none is summed with or relabeled as Expedient construction spending, realized employment, local purchasing, or community benefit.

sources.title: Milwaukee Franklin Data Center specification sheet
sources.notes: The current operator sheet identifies 4777 W Ironwood Drive and reports 27,000 square feet of data-center space, 10,000 square feet of raised floor, 1.6 MW of critical IT load, 3.0 MW of total generator capacity, two auto-cutover diesel generators, and multiple cooling systems. Only the whole-building area and critical-load specifications are normalized here. They are capacity descriptors, not utilization, annual electricity, construction spending, investment, employment, or audited environmental performance.

sources.title: Milwaukee County Public Portal — parcel 9301001000 tax-year 2025
sources.notes: The public parcel-tax page identifies parcel 9301001000, bill 380021, RDC-4777 Ironwood Drive LLC, and 4777 W Ironwood Drive. It reports $66,640.33 gross tax, $6,230.91 school credit, $62.25 first-dollar credit, $60,347.17 net tax, $60,347.17 paid, and zero balance. The payment is a parcel-owner obligation spanning multiple taxing jurisdictions; it is not allocated to Expedient, does not establish an operator reimbursement under the triple-net lease, and supplies no same-scope marginal public-service cost.

sources.title: Connecticut firm buys Franklin data center for $9.5M formerly owned by Harley-Davidson
sources.notes: The article reports that the Franklin data center sold for $9.46 million and attributes the amount to a Wisconsin state record. This is a real-estate ownership transfer after Expedient opened the reused facility, not construction spending, IT-equipment investment, assessed value, tax paid, or an Expedient operating expenditure.

project_updates.title: Post-opening property sale remains an ownership transfer, not project construction spending
project_updates.notes: The reported $9.46 million 2022 sale is retained as an investment-context input only. It is not added to the parcel's assessed value, the 2022 or 2025 permit amounts, property taxes, or Expedient's hiring forecast, and it does not establish local supplier retention or new capital formation.

project_updates.title: Parcel tax paid supports a contribution and break-even threshold, not a net fiscal result
project_updates.notes: The 2025 parcel tax is fully paid, but the public portal does not disclose project-attributable service costs or establish whether Expedient reimbursed the property owner. The account may present the paid parcel tax and an equal same-scope cost break-even threshold, while actual public-service cost and net fiscal position remain unobserved.
